objective: Identify dimensions that give a given number of unit cubes.

stem.en: Which dimensions make a rectangular prism that holds exactly 36 unit cubes?
stem.es: ¿Cuáles dimensiones forman un prisma rectangular que contiene exactamente 36 cubos unitarios?

hints.en: Multiply the three dimensions for each choice.
The product must equal the number of cubes.
Only one choice has a product of exactly 36.

choices.why: 3 × 4 × 4 = 48 cubes, which is too many.
2 × 3 × 5 = 30 cubes, which is too few.
4 × 4 × 2 = 32 cubes, which is too few.

objective: Find the volume of a prism by counting unit cubes in rows, columns and layers.

stem.en: A prism is built from unit cubes. It is 5 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 3 cubes tall. How many unit cubes does it contain?
stem.es: Un prisma se construye con cubos unitarios. Mide 5 cubos de largo, 2 cubos de ancho y 3 cubos de alto. ¿Cuántos cubos unitarios contiene?

hints.en: Count the cubes in one layer first.
A layer that is 5 long and 2 wide has a row of 5 repeated 2 times.
Multiply the cubes in one layer by the number of layers.

solution.es: Una capa tiene 5 × 2 = 10 cubos y 3 capas tienen 30 cubos.

objective: Find the error in counting cubes in layers.

stem.en: Pia counts the cubes in a prism that is 3 cubes long, 4 cubes wide and 2 cubes tall. Step 1: One layer has 3 × 4 = 12 cubes. Step 2: There are 2 layers. Step 3: The total is 12 + 2 = 14 cubes. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Pia cuenta los cubos de un prisma de 3 cubos de largo, 4 cubos de ancho y 2 cubos de alto. Paso 1: One layer has 3 × 4 = 12 cubes. Paso 2: There are 2 layers. Paso 3: The total is 12 + 2 = 14 cubes. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

hints.en: Steps 1 and 2 are correct.
Each layer has 12 cubes.
Do you add or multiply to combine equal layers?

steps: Equal layers are combined by multiplying.
solution.es: Las capas iguales se multiplican: 12 × 2 = 24 cubos.

objective: Find the number of cubes that fill a box from rows and layers.

stem.en: A box is filled with 4 layers of cubes. Each layer has 3 rows with 5 cubes in each row. How many cubes fill the box?
stem.es: Una caja se llena con 4 capas de cubos. Cada capa tiene 3 filas con 5 cubos en cada fila. ¿Cuántos cubos llenan la caja?

hints.en: First find how many cubes are in one layer.
One layer has 3 rows of 5.
Then count all 4 layers.

solution.es: Una capa tiene 15 cubos y 4 capas tienen 60 cubos.

choices.why: This adds 4 + 3 + 5. The cubes are in equal groups, so multiply.
This is the number of cubes in just one layer.

objective: Reason about how volume changes when every dimension is doubled.

stem.en: A box is 2 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm. A second box has every dimension doubled. Does the second box hold twice as much? Find both volumes and explain.
stem.es: Una caja mide 2 cm por 3 cm por 4 cm. Una segunda caja tiene todas las dimensiones duplicadas. ¿Cabe el doble en la segunda caja? Halla ambos volúmenes y explica.

hints.en: Find the volume of each box separately.
Divide the larger volume by the smaller.
Think about how many dimensions were doubled.

solution.es: El segundo volumen es 192 y el primero 24: 192 ÷ 24 = 8 veces.

criteria.en: Finds the first volume 24 cubic centimeters
criteria.es: Halla el primer volumen 24 centímetros cúbicos
Halla el segundo volumen 4 × 6 × 8 = 192

criteria.en: Says it holds 8 times as much, because each of the 3 dimensions doubles
criteria.es: Dice que cabe 8 veces más, porque cada una de las 3 dimensiones se duplica

sample.en: The first box is 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 cm³. The second is 4 × 6 × 8 = 192 cm³. 192 ÷ 24 = 8, so it holds 8 times as much, not 2 times, because length, width and height each double: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.

objective: Identify amounts equal to a mass in a different metric unit.

stem.en: Select ALL the amounts that are equal to 2.5 kilograms.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las cantidades que son iguales a 2.5 kilogramos.

Three of the five choices are equal to 2.5 kg.

25,000 g is 25 kg, 10 times too large.

objective: Explain why volume is measured in cubic units.

stem.en: Explain why volume is measured in cubic units while area is measured in square units.
stem.es: Explica por qué el volumen se mide en unidades cúbicas mientras que el área se mide en unidades cuadradas.

hints.en: What shape do you use to cover a flat surface?
What shape do you use to fill a box?
Count how many directions each unit extends.

steps: Area uses squares to cover a surface (2 dimensions).
Volume uses cubes to fill a solid (3 dimensions).
solution.es: El área usa cuadrados (2 dimensiones) y el volumen usa cubos (3 dimensiones).

criteria.en: Says area counts squares that cover a flat surface
criteria.es: Dice que el área cuenta cuadrados que cubren una superficie plana

criteria.en: Says volume counts cubes that fill a solid
criteria.es: Dice que el volumen cuenta cubos que llenan un sólido

criteria.en: Connects to the number of dimensions (2 and 3)
criteria.es: Relaciona con el número de dimensiones (2 y 3)

sample.en: Area covers a flat surface with squares, which have 2 dimensions. Volume fills a solid with cubes, which have 3 dimensions, so volume uses cubic units.
sample.es: El área cubre una superficie plana con cuadrados, que tienen 2 dimensiones. El volumen llena un sólido con cubos, que tienen 3 dimensiones, así que el volumen usa unidades cúbicas.

objective: Convert a mixed-number length from feet to inches.

What is the height of the water?
Multiply length, width and water depth.

stem.en: Which rectangular prism has the greatest volume?
stem.es: ¿Cuál prisma rectangular tiene el mayor volumen?

stem.en: A bag of flour has a mass of 3.5 kilograms. What is its mass in grams?
stem.es: Una bolsa de harina tiene una masa de 3.5 kilogramos. ¿Cuál es su masa en gramos?

hints.en: There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram.

objective: Redistribute fractional amounts from a data set equally.

stem.en: A line plot shows 5 beakers that hold 1/2, 1/4, 1/4, 3/4 and 1/4 liter of water. All the water is poured out and shared equally among the 5 beakers. How much water is in each beaker?

hints.en: Each dot is one leaf, so multiply the length by the number of dots.
Write all the amounts in fourths.
Add the fourths.

hints.en: Which dots are above numbers greater than 1/4?
Do not count the dots at 1/4.
Add the dots above 1/2 and the dots above 3/4.

That counts only the pieces at 1/2 inch. The piece at 3/4 inch is also longer than 1/4.

sample.en: 5/4 is greater than 1, so 7/8 × 5/4 stretches 7/8 to something larger. Check: 7/8 × 5/4 = 35/32, and 35/32 is more than 28/32, which is 7/8.
sample.es: 5/4 es mayor que 1, así que 7/8 × 5/4 agranda 7/8. Comprobación: 7/8 × 5/4 = 35/32, y 35/32 es más que 28/32, que es 7/8.

objective: Compare products by reasoning about the size of the second factor.

stem.en: Think about the size of the second factor. Which product will be the greatest?
stem.es: Piensa en el tamaño del segundo factor. ¿Cuál producto será el mayor?

hints.en: Compare each second factor with 1.
Multiplying by a number greater than 1 makes the product larger.
Only one of the second factors is greater than 1.

steps: 5/4 is greater than 1, so 3/4 × 5/4 is larger than 3/4.
The other factors are 1 or less, so their products are 3/4 or less.
solution.es: 5/4 es mayor que 1, así que 3/4 × 5/4 es mayor que 3/4.

choices.why: 2/3 is less than 1, so this product is smaller than 3/4.
Multiplying by 1 leaves 3/4 unchanged. It is not greater than 3/4.
4/5 is less than 1, so this product is smaller than 3/4.

objective: Identify products that are less than the first factor without computing.

stem.en: Select ALL the products that are less than 8.
stem.es: Selecciona TODOS los productos que son menores que 8.

hints.en: Compare each fraction with 1.
A number less than 1 shrinks 8.
Two of the five choices shrink 8.

solution.es: 5/6 y 7/10 son menores que 1, por eso esos productos son menores que 8.

choices.why: 3/2 is greater than 1, so the product is greater than 8.
Multiplying by 1 gives 8, which is not less than 8.
9/8 is greater than 1, so the product is greater than 8.

verify.note: Reasons about factor size relative to 1 without computing, so it needs human review.

objective: Resize a quantity by a fraction less than 1.

stem.en: A designer shrinks a logo that is 12 inches wide to 3/4 of its width. How wide is the new logo?
stem.es: Una diseñadora reduce un logotipo de 12 pulgadas de ancho a 3/4 de su ancho. ¿Cuánto mide de ancho el nuevo logotipo?

hints.en: 3/4 of the width means multiply by 3/4.
Find 1/4 of 12 first.
Then take 3 of those parts.

objective: Apply scaling by a fraction to find a model length.

stem.en: A model plane is 2/5 as long as the real plane. The real plane is 30 feet long. How long is the model?
stem.es: Un avión a escala es 2/5 de la longitud del avión real. El avión real mide 30 pies. ¿Cuánto mide el modelo?

hints.en: The model is a fraction of the real length.
Find 1/5 of 30.
Then take 2 of those parts.

criteria.es: Multiplica 30 por 2/5

criteria.en: Finds 12 feet and notes it is less than 30
criteria.es: Halla 12 pies y nota que es menor que 30

sample.en: 2/5 × 30 = 12 feet. The model is shorter than the real plane because 2/5 is less than 1.
sample.es: 2/5 × 30 = 12 pies. El modelo es más corto que el avión real porque 2/5 es menor que 1.

objective: Explain the link between dividing by a unit fraction and multiplying.

stem.en: How many 1/3-cup scoops fill 4 cups? Write a division equation and a multiplication equation that give the same answer, and explain why they match.
stem.es: ¿Cuántas cucharadas de 1/3 de taza llenan 4 tazas? Escribe una ecuación de división y una de multiplicación que den la misma respuesta, y explica por qué coinciden.

hints.en: How many thirds are in 1 cup?
Count the thirds in 4 cups.
Write both a division and a multiplication for that count.

criteria.es: Escribe 4 ÷ 1/3 = 12
Escribe 4 × 3 = 12

criteria.en: Explains that each cup holds 3 thirds
criteria.es: Explica que cada taza tiene 3 tercios

sample.en: 4 ÷ 1/3 = 12 and 4 × 3 = 12. Each cup holds 3 scoops of 1/3, so 4 cups hold 4 × 3 = 12 scoops.
sample.es: 4 ÷ 1/3 = 12 y 4 × 3 = 12. Cada taza tiene 3 cucharadas de 1/3, así que 4 tazas tienen 4 × 3 = 12 cucharadas.

objective: Find the error when writing a division as a fraction.

stem.en: Lena shares 3 granola bars equally among 2 friends. Step 1: She writes the division 3 ÷ 2. Step 2: She writes 3 ÷ 2 = 2/3. Step 3: Each friend gets 2/3 of a bar. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Lena reparte 3 barras de granola por igual entre 2 amigos. Paso 1: She writes the division 3 ÷ 2. Paso 2: She writes 3 ÷ 2 = 2/3. Paso 3: Each friend gets 2/3 of a bar. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

hints.en: Which number is being divided?
Each friend should get more than 1 bar, since 3 bars shared by 2 is more than one each.
Is 2/3 more than 1?

solution.es: 3 ÷ 2 = 3/2, o sea 1 1/2 barras para cada amigo.

steps: Each friend gets 2/3 of a bar.

objective: Solve an equation that multiplies an unknown by a fraction.

stem.en: Three fourths of the cookies in a jar is 6 cookies. Solve 3/4 × n = 6 to find how many cookies n are in the full jar.
stem.es: Tres cuartos de las galletas de un frasco son 6 galletas. Resuelve 3/4 × n = 6 para hallar cuántas galletas n hay en el frasco lleno.

hints.en: If 3 of 4 equal parts are 6 cookies, how many are in each part?
Find the amount in one fourth.
Then multiply by 4 to find all the fourths.

solution.es: Si 3 cuartos son 6, un cuarto es 2 y n = 4 × 2 = 8.

objective: Sort sums of unlike fractions by comparing with 1.

stem.en: Sort each sum by whether it is less than 1 or at least 1.
stem.es: Clasifica cada suma según sea menor que 1 o por lo menos 1.

hints.en: Find each sum using a common denominator.
Compare each sum with 1 whole.
5/8 + 3/8 is exactly 8/8.

solution.es: Las sumas 5/6, 13/20 y 5/12 son menores que 1; 5/4, 1 y 7/6 son por lo menos 1.

objective: Write and solve a story problem for a fraction subtraction.

stem.en: Write a short story problem that matches 3/4 − 1/3. Then solve it and show your work.
stem.es: Escribe un problema con una historia corta que corresponda a 3/4 − 1/3. Luego resuélvelo y muestra tu trabajo.

hints.en: The story must start with 3/4 of something.
Something is taken away, so the story is about subtraction.
Solve using twelfths.

criteria.en: Writes a story that really means taking 1/3 away from 3/4
criteria.es: Escribe una historia que realmente quita 1/3 de 3/4
Reescribe con un denominador común: 9/12 − 4/12
Obtiene 5/12 con unidades

sample.en: A rope is 3/4 yard long. Jo cuts off 1/3 yard. How much is left? 9/12 − 4/12 = 5/12 yard.
sample.es: Una cuerda mide 3/4 de yarda. Jo corta 1/3 de yarda. ¿Cuánto queda? 9/12 − 4/12 = 5/12 de yarda.

objective: Subtract fractions with unlike denominators.

stem.en: There is 7/8 of a loaf of bread. Sam eats 1/4 of a loaf. How much bread is left?
stem.es: Queda 7/8 de una barra de pan. Sam come 1/4 de una barra. ¿Cuánto pan queda?

hints.en: Eighths and fourths can use the same size piece.
Rewrite 1/4 as eighths.
Subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.

objective: Solve a multistep fraction problem and compare with a given amount.

stem.en: A cookie recipe needs 2/3 cup of sugar and a muffin recipe needs 3/4 cup. A baker wants to make 2 batches of each, but has only 2 cups of sugar. How many cups of sugar is the baker short?
stem.es: Una receta de galletas necesita 2/3 de taza de azúcar y una receta de panecillos necesita 3/4 de taza. Un panadero quiere hacer 2 tandas de cada una, pero solo tiene 2 tazas de azúcar. ¿Cuántas tazas de azúcar le faltan?

hints.en: Find how much sugar one cookie batch and one muffin batch use together.
Then double that amount.
Compare the total with 2 cups and find the difference.

solution.es: Necesita 17/6 tazas; tiene 2 = 12/6, así que le faltan 5/6.

criteria.en: Finds sugar for one batch of each: 2/3 + 3/4 = 17/12
criteria.es: Halla el azúcar para una tanda de cada una: 2/3 + 3/4 = 17/12
Lo duplica y obtiene 17/6 de taza

criteria.en: Subtracts 2 cups to find 5/6 cup short
criteria.es: Resta 2 tazas y halla que faltan 5/6 de taza

sample.en: 2/3 + 3/4 = 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12. Two batches need 34/12 = 17/6 cups. 17/6 − 12/6 = 5/6, so the baker is 5/6 cup short.
sample.es: 2/3 + 3/4 = 8/12 + 9/12 = 17/12. Dos tandas necesitan 34/12 = 17/6 tazas. 17/6 − 12/6 = 5/6, así que le faltan 5/6 de taza.

objective: Choose the correct amount when a container is partly full.

stem.en: A tank holds 12 gallons when it is full. It is 5/8 full. How many gallons of water are in the tank?
stem.es: Un tanque contiene 12 galones cuando está lleno. Está lleno hasta 5/8. ¿Cuántos galones de agua hay en el tanque?

hints.en: The tank is 5/8 of 12 gallons.
The answer must be less than 12.
12 × 5 = 60, then divide by 8.

choices.why: This divides 12 by 5/8. The tank is only part full, so the amount is less than 12.
This multiplies 12 × 5 and ignores the 8 in 5/8.

objective: Solve a fraction addition story with unlike denominators.

stem.en: A nature trail has two sections. One section is 3/4 mile long and the other is 5/6 mile long. How long is the whole trail?
stem.es: Un sendero tiene dos secciones. Una mide 3/4 de milla y la otra mide 5/6 de milla. ¿Cuánto mide todo el sendero?

hints.en: Find a size of piece that fits both fourths and sixths.
Twelve is a multiple of both 4 and 6.
Rewrite each fraction in twelfths and add.

criteria.es: Usa un denominador común de 12
Halla 19/12 de milla (1 7/12)

objective: Write contexts that distinguish dividing a unit fraction by a whole number from dividing a whole number by a unit fraction.

stem.en: Write one short story for (1/4) ÷ 3 and another for 3 ÷ (1/4). Solve each one and explain why the two answers are so different.
stem.es: Escribe una historia corta para (1/4) ÷ 3 y otra para 3 ÷ (1/4). Resuelve cada una y explica por qué las dos respuestas son tan distintas.

hints.en: One story is about sharing a small amount; the other is about counting how many small amounts fit.
Cut each fourth into 3 pieces for the first; count the fourths in 3 wholes for the second.
Compare the sizes of the two answers.

steps: One splits a fourth into smaller parts; the other counts fourths in 3 wholes.
solution.es: (1/4) ÷ 3 = 1/12 y 3 ÷ (1/4) = 12; una reparte y la otra cuenta.

criteria.en: Writes a story where 1/4 of something is split into 3 equal parts and finds 1/12
criteria.es: Escribe una historia donde 1/4 de algo se reparte en 3 partes iguales y halla 1/12

criteria.en: Writes a story asking how many fourths are in 3 and finds 12
criteria.es: Escribe una historia que pregunta cuántos cuartos hay en 3 y halla 12

criteria.en: Explains that splitting a small amount makes it smaller while counting fourths in 3 wholes makes a big count
criteria.es: Explica que repartir una cantidad pequeña la hace más pequeña y que contar cuartos en 3 enteros da un número grande

sample.en: Story 1: 1/4 of a pizza is shared by 3 friends, so each gets 1/12 of the pizza. Story 2: How many 1/4-cup scoops fit in 3 cups? 3 × 4 = 12 scoops. In the first story a small piece gets cut into smaller pieces. In the second I count how many small pieces fit in a bigger amount.
sample.es: Historia 1: 1/4 de una pizza se reparte entre 3 amigos, y cada uno recibe 1/12 de la pizza. Historia 2: ¿Cuántas cucharadas de 1/4 de taza caben en 3 tazas? 3 × 4 = 12 cucharadas. En la primera historia un trozo pequeño se corta en trozos más pequeños. En la segunda cuento cuántos trozos pequeños caben en una cantidad mayor.

objective: Divide a unit fraction by a whole number.

stem.en: Four friends share 1/3 of a pie equally. What fraction of the whole pie does each friend get?
stem.es: Cuatro amigos se reparten 1/3 de un pastel por igual. ¿Qué fracción del pastel entero recibe cada amigo?

hints.en: Each third is cut into 4 equal parts.
How many of these small pieces would fill the whole pie?
Multiply the denominators.

objective: Add mixed numbers in a word problem.

stem.en: Leo walked 1 1/2 miles to the park and 2 2/3 miles around it. How far did he walk in all? Give your answer as a fraction.
stem.es: Leo caminó 1 1/2 millas hasta el parque y 2 2/3 millas alrededor de él. ¿Cuánto caminó en total? Da tu respuesta como fracción.

hints.en: Add the wholes and the fractions separately, or rewrite both as fractions greater than 1.
Use sixths for halves and thirds.
Combine all the sixths.

objective: Find a fraction of a mixed-number length.

stem.en: A wall is 3 1/3 meters long. So far, 3/5 of the length has been painted. How many meters have been painted?
stem.es: Una pared mide 3 1/3 metros de largo. Hasta ahora se ha pintado 3/5 de la longitud. ¿Cuántos metros se han pintado?

hints.en: '3/5 of the length' means multiply.
Rewrite 3 1/3 as thirds.
Look for numbers that cancel before you multiply.

criteria.es: Reescribe 3 1/3 como 10/3
Halla 10/3 × 3/5 = 2 metros

objective: Divide a whole number by a unit fraction.

stem.en: A scoop holds 1/2 cup. How many scoops does it take to fill 5 cups of rice?
stem.es: Una cuchara mide 1/2 taza. ¿Cuántas cucharadas se necesitan para llenar 5 tazas de arroz?

hints.en: How many halves are in 1 cup?
Multiply that by the 5 cups.
5 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 5.

steps: There are 2 halves in each cup.
solution.es: Hay 2 mitades en cada taza: 5 × 2 = 10 cucharadas.

objective: Multiply a whole number by a fraction.

stem.en: Seven friends each drink 3/4 cup of juice. How many cups of juice do they drink altogether? Give your answer as a fraction.
stem.es: Siete amigos beben cada uno 3/4 de taza de jugo. ¿Cuántas tazas de jugo beben en total? Da tu respuesta como fracción.

hints.en: There are 7 equal groups of 3/4.
7 times 3 fourths is how many fourths?
Write the total number of fourths over 4.

objective: Generate terms of a numerical pattern from a rule.

stem.en: Rule A: start at 0 and add 3. Rule B: start at 0 and add 6. What number is in Rule B after 5 additions?
stem.es: Regla A: empieza en 0 y suma 3. Regla B: empieza en 0 y suma 6. ¿Qué número hay en la Regla B después de 5 sumas?

hints.en: Rule B adds the same amount each time.
Skip count by the amount Rule B adds.
Keep adding that amount five times.

solution.es: Regla B: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30; después de 5 sumas hay 30.

objective: Analyze the relationship between corresponding terms and critique a claim.

stem.en: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 5. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 10. Ana says, 'Each B term is 5 more than its matching A term.' Is she right? Use the third and fourth terms to explain.
stem.es: El patrón A empieza en 0 y suma 5. El patrón B empieza en 0 y suma 10. Ana dice: 'Cada término de B es 5 más que su término correspondiente de A'. ¿Tiene razón? Usa el tercer y el cuarto término para explicar.

hints.en: Write out the first four terms of each pattern.
Subtract matching terms. Is the difference always the same?
Try dividing matching terms to find the real relationship.

steps: 20 − 10 = 10 and 30 − 15 = 15, so the difference is not always 5.
solution.es: La diferencia crece; en cambio cada término de B es 2 veces el de A.

criteria.en: Finds the third terms 10 and 20 and the fourth terms 15 and 30
criteria.es: Halla los terceros términos 10 y 20 y los cuartos términos 15 y 30

criteria.en: Shows the difference is not always 5
criteria.es: Muestra que la diferencia no siempre es 5

criteria.en: States each B term is 2 times its A term
criteria.es: Dice que cada término de B es 2 veces el de A

sample.en: No. The third terms are 10 and 20, which differ by 10. The fourth terms are 15 and 30, which differ by 15. Each B term is 2 times the A term.
sample.es: No. Los terceros términos son 10 y 20, que difieren en 10. Los cuartos términos son 15 y 30, que difieren en 15. Cada término de B es 2 veces el de A.

objective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses, brackets and braces.

hints.en: Start with the symbols that are nested deepest.
Inside the brackets, divide after you finish the parentheses.
Finish the braces, then multiply the result by 2.

objective: Find the error in a claim about two patterns.

stem.en: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 3. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 9. Step 1: A is 0, 3, 6, 9 and B is 0, 9, 18, 27. Step 2: The third terms are 6 and 18, and 18 − 6 = 12. Step 3: The fourth terms are 9 and 27, and 27 − 9 = 18. Step 4: So each B term is always 12 more than its A term. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: El patrón A empieza en 0 y suma 3. El patrón B empieza en 0 y suma 9. Paso 1: A is 0, 3, 6, 9 and B is 0, 9, 18, 27. Paso 2: The third terms are 6 and 18, and 18 − 6 = 12. Paso 3: The fourth terms are 9 and 27, and 27 − 9 = 18. Paso 4: So each B term is always 12 more than its A term. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

hints.en: Compare the differences Sam found in steps 2 and 3.
A rule that is always true must give the same difference every time.
Look for a different relationship, such as multiplying.

steps: The differences are 12 and 18, so they are not always 12.
Each B term is 3 times its A term: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 and 27 ÷ 9 = 3.
solution.es: Las diferencias son 12 y 18; en realidad cada término de B es 3 veces el de A.

steps: The third terms are 6 and 18, and 18 − 6 = 12.
The fourth terms are 9 and 27, and 27 − 9 = 18.
So each B term is always 12 more than its A term.

objective: Identify all expressions with the same value, including brackets and parentheses.

stem.en: Select ALL the expressions that have a value of 24.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las expresiones que tienen un valor de 24.

hints.en: Find the value of each choice separately.
Do the grouping symbols first in every choice.
Three of the five choices have the same value.

choices.why: Multiply first: 6 + 6 = 12.
Multiply 2 × 6 first: 3 + 12 = 15.

objective: Interpret a numerical expression without evaluating it.

stem.en: Mia wrote 2 × (14 + 9). Which sentence describes her expression?
stem.es: Mia escribió 2 × (14 + 9). ¿Qué oración describe su expresión?

hints.en: Find the part inside the parentheses first.
Read what the × 2 does to that part.
Say it in words: 2 times what?

steps: Inside the parentheses is the sum of 14 and 9.
The 2 × means twice that whole sum.
solution.es: Es el doble de la suma de 14 y 9.

choices.why: Here only the 9 is doubled. In Mia's expression the whole sum 14 + 9 is doubled.

text.en: Two more than the sum of 14 and 9
text.es: Two more than the sum of 14 and 9

choices.why: 'Two more than' would use addition: 2 + (14 + 9).

text.en: The sum of 14 and 9, divided by 2
text.es: The sum of 14 and 9, divided by 2

choices.why: The expression multiplies by 2, not divides.

verify.note: Matches words to an expression without computing anything, so it needs human review.

objective: Build an expression with grouping symbols that reaches a target value using given numbers.

stem.en: Use each of the numbers 2, 3, 4 and 5 exactly once, with any of + − × ÷ and parentheses, to write an expression with a value of 20. Show that its value is 20.
stem.es: Usa cada uno de los números 2, 3, 4 y 5 exactamente una vez, con cualquiera de + − × ÷ y paréntesis, para escribir una expresión con un valor de 20. Muestra que su valor es 20.

hints.en: Think about which two numbers multiply to 20 or close to it.
Can the other two numbers make a 1 or another helpful number?
Use parentheses so the leftover pair is combined first.

criteria.en: Uses each of 2, 3, 4 and 5 exactly once
criteria.es: Usa cada uno de 2, 3, 4 y 5 exactamente una vez
Usa los paréntesis correctamente

criteria.en: Shows the evaluation steps and gets 20
criteria.es: Muestra los pasos de la evaluación y obtiene 20

objective: Write and evaluate an expression for a multistep story.

stem.en: Dev buys 3 packs of markers with 8 markers in each pack. He also has 5 loose markers. Then he gives 7 markers to a friend. How many markers does Dev have now?
stem.es: Dev compra 3 paquetes de marcadores con 8 marcadores en cada paquete. También tiene 5 marcadores sueltos. Luego le da 7 marcadores a un amigo. ¿Cuántos marcadores tiene Dev ahora?

hints.en: Start by finding how many markers are in the packs.
Then add the loose markers and take away the ones given away.
Write one expression that matches the story, then evaluate it.

criteria.es: Escribe una expresión como 3 × 8 + 5 − 7
Halla 22 marcadores

objective: Match expressions with grouping symbols to their values.

stem.en: Match each expression to its value.
stem.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su valor.

hints.en: Find the value of one expression at a time.
Watch where the parentheses are. They show what to do first.
Two expressions use the same numbers but give different values.

objective: Evaluate an expression with parentheses and brackets.

stem.en: Work from the inside out to evaluate the expression 4 × [18 − (3 + 5)].
stem.es: Trabaja de adentro hacia afuera para evaluar la expresión 4 × [18 − (3 + 5)].

hints.en: Work inside the innermost grouping symbols first.
Finish everything inside the brackets before you multiply.
Add 3 + 5, then subtract that from 18, then multiply by 4.

objective: Find a missing term of an ordered pair from a pattern in a table of pairs.

stem.en: The ordered pairs (1, 4), (2, 8) and (3, 12) follow a rule. Using the same rule, what is the second number when the first number is 9?
stem.es: Los pares ordenados (1, 4), (2, 8) y (3, 12) siguen una regla. Con la misma regla, ¿cuál es el segundo número cuando el primer número es 9?

hints.en: Look at how each second number compares with its first number.
Each second number is the first number multiplied by the same amount.
Use that same multiplier on the first number 9.

steps: 4 = 1 × 4, 8 = 2 × 4, 12 = 3 × 4, so the rule is multiply by 4.
solution.es: La regla es multiplicar por 4, entonces 9 × 4 = 36.

objective: Recognize which expression is not equivalent to a given expression.

stem.en: Which expression does NOT have the same value as 2 × (6 + 9)?
stem.es: ¿Cuál expresión NO tiene el mismo valor que 2 × (6 + 9)?

hints.en: First find the value of 2 × (6 + 9).
Find the value of each choice and compare.
One choice doubles only the 6.

choices.why: 6 + 9 = 15, so this is the same as 2 × (6 + 9). Both equal 30.
Both parts are doubled: 12 + 18 = 30, the same value.
Adding the sum to itself is twice the sum: 30.

objective: Identify an ordered pair that fits the relationship between two patterns.

stem.en: The first numbers start at 0 and add 5. The second numbers start at 0 and add 15. Which ordered pair belongs to this pattern?
stem.es: Los primeros números empiezan en 0 y suman 5. Los segundos números empiezan en 0 y suman 15. ¿Qué par ordenado pertenece a este patrón?

hints.en: Find the first few pairs: (0, 0), (5, 15) and so on.
Compare each second number with its first number.
Look for the pair where the second number is 3 times the first.

solution.es: El par (10, 30) está en el patrón: 30 es 3 veces 10.

choices.why: The second number here is only 2 times the first. In this pattern it is 3 times the first.
The second number here is 2 times the first, not 3 times.
The second number is not a whole-number multiple of 20. It should be 3 times as large.

objective: Explain how parentheses change the value of an expression.

stem.en: Do 6 × (10 − 4) and 6 × 10 − 4 have the same value? Find both values and explain what the parentheses change.
stem.es: ¿Tienen 6 × (10 − 4) y 6 × 10 − 4 el mismo valor? Halla ambos valores y explica qué cambian los paréntesis.

hints.en: Find the value of each expression by itself.
In one expression, 10 − 4 is done first. In the other, 6 × 10 is.
Compare the two values, then say why they differ.

steps: Parentheses change which operation happens first.
solution.es: 36 y 56 son diferentes porque los paréntesis cambian qué operación se hace primero.

criteria.en: Says the parentheses make you subtract before multiplying
criteria.es: Dice que los paréntesis hacen restar antes de multiplicar

sample.en: No. 6 × (10 − 4) = 6 × 6 = 36, but 6 × 10 − 4 = 60 − 4 = 56. The parentheses make you subtract first.
sample.es: No. 6 × (10 − 4) = 6 × 6 = 36, pero 6 × 10 − 4 = 60 − 4 = 56. Los paréntesis hacen restar primero.

objective: Find the error in evaluating an expression that has parentheses and mixed operations.

stem.en: Dev evaluated 30 − (4 + 6) × 2. Step 1: 30 − (4 + 6) × 2 Step 2: 30 − 10 × 2 Step 3: 20 × 2 Step 4: 40 Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Dev evaluó 30 − (4 + 6) × 2. Paso 1: 30 − (4 + 6) × 2 Paso 2: 30 − 10 × 2 Paso 3: 20 × 2 Paso 4: 40 ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

hints.en: Multiplication is done before subtraction unless parentheses say otherwise.
Look at what Dev did first after finishing the parentheses.
Check the step where 30 − 10 turned into 20.

objective: Place parentheses in an expression to make a target value.

stem.en: Where can one pair of parentheses go in 5 + 3 × 4 − 2 so the value is 30?
stem.es: ¿Dónde puede ir un par de paréntesis en 5 + 3 × 4 − 2 para que el valor sea 30?

hints.en: Parentheses are most useful when they change what happens first.
To reach a big value, try adding 5 and 3 before multiplying.
Test the choice that groups the first two numbers.

choices.why: These parentheses group what already happens first. The value stays 15.
This gives 5 + 3 × 2 = 11.
Multiplication already comes first inside, so the value is 15.

objective: Choose the expression whose value is given, using the order of operations with parentheses.

stem.en: Which expression has a value of 22?
stem.es: ¿Cuál expresión tiene un valor de 22?

hints.en: Work out each choice one at a time.

solution.es: Restar 4 de 20 es 20 − 4; luego se divide: (20 − 4) ÷ 2.
